newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Result of SFO probe into Maori TV weeks away.
newsitem.headline: Result of SFO probe into Maori TV weeks away.

text.p: An investigation into pilot Maori Television broadcaster Aotearoa Television Network (ATN) would be completed in a matter of weeks, the Serious Fraud Office said on Thursday.

"We expect the investigation to probably be concluded in a number of weeks. Weeks rather than months," SFO associate director, investigations Gib Beattie told parliament's Justice and Law Reform committee.

The government in March withdrew NZ$4 million funding set aside for ATN pending an investigation into the station's financial affairs. The decision follows widespread publicity about spending on clothes by two ATN directors, property deals, and the board of directors' lack of management of the station.
Opposition MPs have raised questions about whether New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan had a financial interest in the station after he resigned as a director last year.
Morgan, who was subsequently elected to parliament for the Te Tai Hauauru seat, has denied the allegations.
Acting SFO director David Bradshaw would not comment on details of the SFO inquiry.
"We are not able to talk about the conduct or course of any investigation," Bradshaw said.
Earlier Bradshaw had told the committee he had been seconded to the SFO as acting director for three weeks while Director Charles Sturt was on sick leave.
